To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“whaling tradition has an important influence on the public perception of cetaces in coastal areas, but not in inland provinces”.
the whaling tradition has a relevant influence on the perception of the inhabitants of coastal areas, and that this perception is not always positive.

1) Whaling has a relevant cultural imprint on the inhabitants of the Cantabrian coasts, and this is reflected in the public perception of cetaces; 2) Inhabitants from coastal regions with a whaling tradition showed higher levels of knowledge, more negative attitudes, and less willingness to take action than respondents from inland areas; and 3) Gender and age are also important factors that influence public perception of cetacea and whales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of considering the cultural and historical context of the study area in order to design effective conservation policies and to achieve real and sustainable marine citizenship.
the need of taking into account the local context and the history of the region when designing conservation programmes.
the importance of understanding public perception of cetacians and whaling in order to promote marine conservation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, despite the fact that the inhabitants of the North of Spain are very familiar with whaling, their knowledge about cetacean species and their protection is very limited.
the whaling tradition along the coast is still present in the public perception of cetacians and that it is important for marine conservation.
, in order to achieve a real marine conservation, the public perception of cetacea and the whaling activity must be taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the whaling history of a certain region can influence the perception of its inhabitants towards cetaceans, and that it is necessary to take this into account in conservation programmes.

, in the case of the North Atlantic Right Whale, the history of whaling has a significant impact in the perception of this species by coastal inhabitants, but it is not enough to ensure a positive attitude towards its conservation.
the whaling tradition is still a relevant cultural heritage along the Cantabian coast, and it has a significant impact on the perception of citizens towards cetaceans.
